subject: Pilot economics and PO threshold - commit spectrum & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Park <dana@acmesoft.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T15:12:00+00:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — pilot economics + procurement path

Hi Dana — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can get the pilot in motion:

What we heard (your team):
- Expected monthly token range for the first 6 months: ~200M–350M tokens (peak bursts may exceed this briefly).
- Primary success criteria: latency under 250ms p50 for chat flows, production-quality outputs for 3 specific intents you shared.
- Procurement note: finance handles POs under $50k; anything above triggers vendor onboarding and a legal review (per Dana).

Initial Redwood proposal (two options):
1) Pilot (staged, month-to-month): 12-week pilot with an initial monthly commitment of 50M tokens, billed monthly at a test rate of $140 / 1M tokens. This keeps near-term spend under procurement thresholds while giving us signal.
2) Committed annual lane (preferred for unit economics): 12-month commit with monthly delivery; committed rate target $95 / 1M tokens for volumes in the 200M–350M band. Example math at 250M tokens/mo -> ~$23,750 / month.

Questions / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm the 200M–350M monthly estimate (range is fine) so we can size the committed band?
2) Is AcmeSoft comfortable with a 12-week pilot at the proposed test rate, with the option to convert to a committed plan at the $95 / 1M rate once you sign a PO/IO?
3) Procurement gate: you mentioned <= $50k is fast-path. If we structure the pilot to keep month 1 under that, would procurement be able to process without vendor registration?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short IO + one-page SOW that mirrors the pilot scope and shows sample invoices. (attached: Redwood-Proposal-AcmeSoft-v2.pdf, IO-template.docx)
- If you confirm the token range and procurement fast-path, we’ll schedule a kickoff for the week of Nov 13.

Thanks — cc’ing Grace to help with SOW and finance details on our side.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dana Park <dana@acmesoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — pilot economics + procurement path

Thanks Karthik — quick answers from our side:

- Token range: yes, 200M–350M per month is our expected window for months 2–6. Month 1 will likely be a smaller ramp (30–60M) while engineering finishes integration.
- Pilot: 12-week pilot at a test rate of $140 / 1M tokens sounds fine. We prefer a pilot IO with a clear conversion path.
- Procurement: correct — purchases under $50k can be done by our internal buyer without full vendor onboarding. Anything above that goes through vendor registration (2–3 week lead) + legal review.

Two asks from us:
1) Can you show the committed-rate math at 200M, 275M, and 350M bands for the $95 / 1M rate so we can present to finance?
2) Please send the IO and a sample invoice so procurement knows what to expect.

I’m cc’ing our procurement address so they have the thread: procurement@acmesoft.com

— Dana
VP, Product Engineering | AcmeSoft
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Finance Team <finance@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T11:30:00+00:00
Subject: Internal: AcmeSoft pilot economics — PO threshold and discount approval

Folks — looping you in for a quick approval path question. AcmeSoft (prospect) has confirmed a projected steady-state window of 200M–350M tokens/month after ramp. They want to pilot first (month 1 = 30–60M), then convert to a committed plan.

Proposal options we discussed with the buyer:
- Pilot IO: 12 weeks, month-to-month for the pilot portion at $140 / 1M tokens. Expected month-1 spend ~ $4.2k–$8.4k (keeps it under Acme's $50k procurement fast path).
- Committed lane: 12-month commitment at $95 / 1M tokens for the 200M–350M band. Example monthly bills:
  • 200M tokens @ $95/1M = $19,000
  • 275M tokens @ $95/1M = $26,125
  • 350M tokens @ $95/1M = $33,250

Questions for finance / deals desk:
1) Can deals desk sign off on a $95 / 1M committed rate for a 12-month IO (monthly invoicing) without escalation? If not, where is the threshold?
2) Is Redwood able to accept a PO/IO where the first 1–2 months remain under the $50k Acme fast-path while future months exceed it? Any implications for vendor onboarding?
3) Approver for a one-time onboarding credit (we were considering $1,500 credit to offset their initial integration costs) — who should sign off?

Cc’ing Monica since she’ll own the negotiated IO. Grace, any immediate items I should adjust in the draft IO?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Park <dana@acmesoft.com>, AcmeSoft Procurement <procurement@acmesoft.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-07T14:45:00+00:00
Subject: Confirmation & next steps — IO + kickoff dates

Hi Dana / Procurement — following internal checks, we’re aligned and ready to proceed. Summary + attachments below:

What we’re proposing:
- 12-week pilot IO (attached) at $140 / 1M tokens for the pilot months. Initial month estimate: 30–60M tokens.
- Conversion path: upon signature of an IO for the committed lane we’ll move to the committed rate of $95 / 1M for the agreed band (200M–350M).
- Billing: monthly invoices; we accept AcmeSoft PO for invoice processing.
- Onboarding credit: Redwood will include a one-time $1,500 integration credit on the first invoice (applied to the pilot).

Attachments sent: Redwood-Proposal-AcmeSoft-v2.pdf, IO-template.docx, pricing-breakdown-20281107.xlsx

Proposed schedule:
- Send signed IO back by Nov 13 to hit a Nov 20 kickoff.
- Engineering kickoff (technical onboarding) week of Nov 20; pilot monitoring/health checks weekly.

Dana — if this matches your expectations, please reply with OK and confirm whether procurement needs any additional vendor paperwork before we send the DocuSign link. Procurement, feel free to request our W-9, SOC 2 attestation (we have reports) or standard vendor packet — we’ll provide quickly.

Thanks — look forward to getting started.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
